text: Dengue is a viral infection spread by mosquitoes. Most people have mild or no symptoms. Common symptoms are high fever, headache, body aches, nausea and rash. Most people get better in 1 to 2 weeks.

Severe dengue warning signs often appear after the fever goes away: severe stomach pain, repeated vomiting, fast breathing, bleeding gums, blood in vomit or stool, tiredness or restlessness. A person with these signs needs hospital care right away.

Lower the risk of dengue by avoiding mosquito bites, especially during the day. There is no specific medicine that cures dengue; care focuses on managing symptoms such as pain. See a doctor if you suspect dengue.

Diabetes is a condition with high blood sugar. Symptoms include feeling very thirsty, urinating often, tiredness, blurred vision and unexplained weight loss. In type 2 diabetes symptoms may be mild or absent for years, so a blood test is the way to find it.

Lifestyle changes are the best way to prevent or delay type 2 diabetes. Care for diabetes includes healthy eating, regular physical activity, checking blood sugar and medicines when a doctor advises. Type 1 diabetes cannot currently be prevented.
Hypertension or high blood pressure means a reading of 140/90 mmHg or higher, confirmed on two different days. Most people feel no symptoms, so the way to know is to have blood pressure measured.
To help lower high blood pressure: eat a healthy diet with less salt, lose excess weight, be physically active and stop tobacco. Some people also need medicines prescribed by a doctor.
Very high blood pressure, usually 180/120 or higher, with severe headache, chest pain, dizziness, difficulty breathing, vision changes or confusion needs care immediately.

The main danger of diarrhoea is dehydration, the loss of water and salts. It is treated with oral rehydration salts (ORS) in clean water. For children, health workers also advise zinc tablets for 10 to 14 days. Severe dehydration may need fluids through a drip.
Diarrhoea often spreads through unsafe food and water. Safe drinking water, good sanitation and washing hands with soap reduce the risk.

Tuberculosis (TB) is a bacterial infection that mostly affects the lungs and spreads through the air. Common symptoms are a long-lasting cough (sometimes with blood), chest pain, weakness, tiredness, weight loss, fever and night sweats. Get tested if you have these.
TB is preventable and curable. It is treated with special antibiotics. Stopping treatment early can lead to drug-resistant TB, so complete the full course your health worker prescribes.
